extracted.intended_audience: Magma users and researchers implementing and simulating error-correcting codes
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and example code for encoding a string into codewords, simulating noisy transmission (component-wise corruption controlled by a noise parameter), optionally decoding the received words, and converting back to a string in Magma. Includes notes on decoding algorithms (Euclidean vs syndrome) and practical handling of unused/illegal codewords.

rubrics_metrics.name: Euclidean versus syndrome decoding trade-off
rubrics_metrics.description: By using Euclidean decoding rather than syndrome decoding, the construction of coset leaders can be avoided. (On the other hand, the coset leaders of a code are stored once they are computed, so it is a once-only time constraint.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Euclidean decoding to avoid the potentially expensive construction of coset leaders and for much faster runtime in examples shown (timings: Euclidean 0.000 vs Syndrome 11.501). However, if syndrome decoding is used the coset leaders need only be computed once and then reused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final phase of decoding: compute information part
rubrics_metrics.description: The final phase in decoding, the computation of the information part of the corrected vector, should be accomplished as demonstrated previously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After computing the corrected codeword vector, extract/compute its information (message) part according to the code's information space/generator matrix as shown in earlier examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Euclidean algorithm error-correcting capacity (Goppa code)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the Goppa code example with r = 3, the Euclidean algorithm is able to correct r/2 = 1 error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When selecting/analysing a Goppa code, use r to determine the error-correcting capability of the Euclidean algorithm (as per the example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Code size requirement for character-by-character ASCII encoding
rubrics_metrics.description: To encode the characters with ASCII codes 1 to 127, a code with at least 127 codewords is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When encoding characters individually map each symbol to a distinct information-space index; ensure the chosen code's information space (number of distinct codewords used) is at least the size of the alphabet being encoded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of code for character encoding (example guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The demo chooses a binary BCH code with n = 15 and d = 5, having 128 codewords, so one of the codewords will not be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer a code whose number of distinct codewords >= alphabet_size; if the code has extra unused codewords, decide and record how to treat them (unused reserved symbol, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: send function interface semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: send(str, noise, decode): str = input string; noise = non-negative number where 0 = perfect transmission, slightly higher values mean some codeword components may be altered, and 1 means every codeword component will be altered; decode = Boolean true iff the Decode algorithm is to be applied. It returns a string of the same length as str which will resemble it depending on noise and decode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design simulation functions with clear parameter semantics: a probabilistic noise parameter in [0,1] interpreted as per-component corruption probability, and a decoding flag controlling whether to apply the decoder to the noisy received words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encode per-character via information-space indices
rubrics_metrics.description: For simplicity, the string is encoded character-by-character: enc := [ wds[STC(str[i])] * GM : i in [1..#str] ]; (wds is sequence of information-space vectors returned from InformationSpace).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement encoding by mapping each character to an index in the information space, then multiplying (or otherwise converting) to the codeword via the generator matrix. Ensure consistent mapping functions StringToCode/CodeToString are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perturbation (noise) model: per-component random alteration
rubrics_metrics.description: The perturbate function flips/changes each codeword component independently with probability equal to noise (implemented as if Random(1000)/1000 le noise then v[i] := v[i] + 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simulate channel noise by independently perturbing each coordinate with probability = noise. Document exactly how a perturbation alters a coordinate (e.g., add 1 modulo field characteristic) so results are reproducible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional decoding step application
rubrics_metrics.description: If decode is true then apply the Decode algorithm to the received vector sequence to obtain corrected codewords, otherwise skip decoding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an option to run or skip decoding to compare raw noisy outputs vs. decoder-corrected outputs; ensure the Decode call's return values (success flags, corrected words) are handled and checked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fallback handling for non-codewords / decoder output
rubrics_metrics.description: Convert non-codewords to the codeword for 'X' (or another designated fallback). Example: Xwd := wds[STC("X")] * GM; corrB := [ v in C select v else Xwd : v in corr ];
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a received or corrected vector is not a valid codeword (or maps to an index outside the intended symbol set), replace it with a designated placeholder codeword to avoid mapping errors when converting back to characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mapping indices back to characters with bounds checking
rubrics_metrics.description: Find index-positions for codewords via Index(wds, InfSp!Coordinates(C, wd)), then convert illegal index-positions of unused codewords to the index for 'x' (xindex := STC("x"); decB := [ i le 127 select i else xindex : i in dec ];).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When converting codewords back to symbols, clamp or remap indices outside the allowed range to a safe fallback symbol to ensure the returned string has valid characters and expected length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Returned string length and resemblance properties
rubrics_metrics.description: send returns a string of the same length as the input; the closeness of the returned string to the original depends on noise and whether decode was applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tests/examples should demonstrate behavior across noise levels and with/without decoding so users understand how decode improves fidelity and at what noise levels decoding degrades.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical example-based validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Example runs (text sample with noise=0.01 or 0.1, decode true/false) illustrate how low noise + decoding recovers original text, while high noise or no decoding produces many placeholder characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include concrete examples and printed outputs to validate implementation and to let users calibrate acceptable noise ranges for their code/decoder choice.
